nodes.title: BLGGT's normalisations of automorphic Galois representations
nodes.statement: Register of the conventions BLGGT (arXiv v4) fixes, against which every ML.2 statement is read. (1) A polarized automorphic representation of GL_n(𝔸_F) is a pair (π, χ) with χ : 𝔸_{F⁺}^×/(F⁺)^× → ℂ^× continuous, χ_v(−1) independent of v | ∞, and π^c ≅ π^∨ ⊗ (χ ∘ N_{F/F⁺} ∘ det), with χ_v(−1) = (−1)^n for v | ∞ when F is imaginary; v4's "polarized" replaces v1's RAECSDC (F imaginary CM) and RAESDC (F totally real). (2) Weights a ∈ (ℤ^n)^{Hom(F,ℂ),+}: π has weight a if π_∞ has the infinitesimal character of Ξ_a^∨; then a ∈ (ℤ^n)_w for some w. (3) The Galois normalisation: (r_{l,ı}(π), ε_l^{1−n}r_{l,ı}(χ)) is totally odd polarized, HT_τ(r_{l,ı}(π)) = {a_{ıτ,1} + n − 1, …, a_{ıτ,n}}, and ıWD(r_{l,ı}(π)|_{G_{F_v}})^{F-ss} ≅ rec(π_v ⊗ |det|_v^{(1−n)/2}) for v ∤ l (and for v | l when π_v has Iwahori-fixed vectors). (4) HT_τ(ε_l) = {−1} and Art_K sends uniformisers to geometric Frobenius. (5) Being automorphic does not depend on ı (Clozel, Theorem 3.13).
hypotheses: F is a CM or totally real field with maximal totally real subfield F⁺; l is a prime and ı : Q̄_l ≅ ℂ; for an imaginary CM F, c ∈ Gal(F/F⁺) is complex conjugation and G_n = (GL_n × GL_1) ⋊ {1, j} is the group of BLGGT §1.1 (CHT08).
proofSteps: Collect the definitions of BLGGT §2.1 and §1 (notation) and compare each with AG2.0's polarized case and AG2.2's realisation; the v1 → v4 renaming (RAECSDC/RAESDC → polarized) is recorded in blggt-version-register.
acceptance: Check the parity condition on an example: for F imaginary CM and n = 2, χ_v(−1) = +1, so ε_l^{−1}r_{l,ı}(χ) is −1 on every complex conjugation (totally odd).
Check the Hodge–Tate normalisation on a weight-0 π: HT_τ = {n − 1, n − 2, …, 0}, n distinct integers.

nodes.title: Polarized l-adic and mod l representations
nodes.statement: A polarized l-adic (resp. mod l) representation of G_F is a pair (r, µ), r : G_F → GL_n(Q̄_l) (resp. GL_n(F̄_l)), µ : G_{F⁺} → Q̄_l^× (resp. F̄_l^×) continuous, such that for some infinite place v of F⁺ there are ε_v ∈ {±1} and a non-degenerate pairing ⟨ , ⟩_v with ⟨x, y⟩_v = ε_v⟨y, x⟩_v and ⟨r(σ)x, r(c_vσc_v)y⟩_v = µ(σ)⟨x, y⟩_v for σ ∈ G_F; for F imaginary, additionally ε_v = −µ(c_v). It is totally odd if ε_v = 1 for all v | ∞; algebraic if r is unramified almost everywhere and de Rham above l; regular algebraic if moreover each HT_τ(r) has n distinct elements. For F imaginary, (r, µ) is polarized iff r extends to r̃ : G_{F⁺} → G_n(Q̄_l) with multiplier µ; for F totally real, iff r factors through GSp_n (µ(c_v) = −ε_v) or GO_n (µ(c_v) = ε_v) with multiplier µ.
hypotheses: F is a CM or totally real field with maximal totally real subfield F⁺; l is a prime and ı : Q̄_l ≅ ℂ; for an imaginary CM F, c ∈ Gal(F/F⁺) is complex conjugation and G_n = (GL_n × GL_1) ⋊ {1, j} is the group of BLGGT §1.1 (CHT08).
proofSteps: Independence of v: ε_{v′} = µ(c_vc_{v′})ε_v and ⟨x, y⟩_{v′} = ⟨x, r(c_vc_{v′})y⟩_v.
The G_n-extension: send c to (A, µ(c))j with A the Gram matrix of ⟨ , ⟩_v (BLGGT §1.1; CHT Lemma 2.1.1).
Totally real case: ⟨x, y⟩ = ⟨x, r(c_v)y⟩_v is G_F-equivariant up to µ.
acceptance: Check that the condition ε_v = −µ(c_v) can always be achieved by replacing µ by µδ_{F/F⁺} (BLGGT p. 31).

nodes.title: Adequate subgroups of GL_n(F̄_l)
nodes.statement: A subgroup H ⊆ GL_n(F̄_l) is adequate if H¹(H, F̄_l) = 0 and H¹(H, sl_n(F̄_l)) = 0, H⁰(H, sl_n(F̄_l)) = 0, and the elements of H of order prime to l span M_n(F̄_l). This is equivalent to Thorne's Definition 2.3 (GHTT Lemma 1). If H is adequate, F̄_l^n is an irreducible H-module and l ∤ n.
hypotheses: l a prime, n ≥ 1, H any subgroup (finite in applications).
proofSteps: Irreducibility from the third condition: an H-stable subspace is stable under the span M_n(F̄_l).
l ∤ n: if l | n then the scalars F̄_l·1_n lie in sl_n and are H-invariant, contradicting H⁰(H, sl_n) = 0.
acceptance: Check the remark l ∤ n on the smallest case: in characteristic 3 the identity of M_3 has trace 0, so scalars lie in sl_3 (suggested file).

sources.match: The definition, the equivalence with Thorne's, and the consequences l ∤ n and irreducibility.

nodes.title: ı-ordinary automorphic representations
nodes.statement: Let π be regular algebraic of weight a, v | l a place, ϖ_v a uniformiser and Iw(v^{b,b}) ⊆ GL_n(O_{F_v}) the matrices unipotent upper-triangular mod v^b. On (ı^{−1}π_v)^{Iw(v^{b,b})} the operators U^{(j)}_{ϖ_v} = [Iw diag(ϖ_v 1_j, 1_{n−j}) Iw] are rescaled to U^{(j)}_{ı*a,ϖ_v} = (∏_{τ:F_v↪Q̄_l}∏_{i=1}^j τ(ϖ_v)^{−a_{ı∘τ|_F, n−i+1}})U^{(j)}_{ϖ_v}; the ordinary part is the largest invariant subspace on which every eigenvalue of every U^{(j)}_{ı*a,ϖ_v} is an l-adic unit, and π is ı-ordinary if for each v | l some b > 0 gives a nonzero ordinary part. This does not depend on ϖ_v; π is ı-ordinary iff π ⊗ (ψ ∘ det) is, for algebraic ψ; weight 0 with π_v Steinberg for all v | l implies ı-ordinary (Geraghty Lemma 5.1.5); ı-ordinary ⇒ r_{l,ı}(π)|_{G_{F_v}} ordinary; level potentially prime to l and r_{l,ı}(π) ordinary ⇒ ı-ordinary.
hypotheses: F is a CM or totally real field with maximal totally real subfield F⁺; l is a prime and ı : Q̄_l ≅ ℂ; for an imaginary CM F, c ∈ Gal(F/F⁺) is complex conjugation and G_n = (GL_n × GL_1) ⋊ {1, j} is the group of BLGGT §1.1 (CHT08).
π a regular algebraic automorphic representation of GL_n(𝔸_F) of weight a.
proofSteps: Changing ϖ_v to ϖ_v′ multiplies U^{(j)} by a commuting operator ⟨u⟩ with ⟨u⟩^b = 1, so the unit-eigenvalue condition is unchanged.
The Galois comparisons are Geraghty's Lemmas 5.1.5, 5.1.6 and 5.2.1 (cited; the twisting argument of BLGHT11 §1).
acceptance: Check the independence of the uniformiser on the rescaling factor: τ(ϖ_v u)^{−a} = τ(ϖ_v)^{−a}τ(u)^{−a}, a unit.

nodes.title: Connecting potentially crystalline lifts: ρ₁ ∼ ρ₂
nodes.statement: For continuous ρ₁, ρ₂ : G_K → GL_n(O_{Q̄_l}), ρ₁ connects to ρ₂ (ρ₁ ∼ ρ₂) iff ρ̄₁ ≅ ρ̄₂, both are potentially crystalline, HT_τ(ρ₁) = HT_τ(ρ₂) for every τ, and ρ₁, ρ₂ define points on the same irreducible component of Spec(R^□_{ρ̄₁,{HT_τ(ρ₁)},K′-cris} ⊗ Q̄_l) for all sufficiently large K′. It does not depend on the identification of the reductions or on GL_n(O)-conjugation; it is an equivalence relation; ρ₁ ∼ ρ₂ implies WD(ρ₁)|_{I_K} ≅ WD(ρ₂)|_{I_K}; it is preserved by restriction to G_{K′}, ⊕, ⊗ and duals; ρ₁ ∼ ρ₁ ⊗ µ for µ unramified with µ̄ = 1; and if ρ̄₁ is semisimple and Fil^i is an invariant filtration by direct summands then ρ₁ ∼ ⊕_i gr^iρ₁ (remarks (1)–(7)).
hypotheses: K/Q_l finite (the case l = p of BLGGT §1.4); O the integers of a finite L/Q_l containing all embeddings of K; for multisets {H_τ} of n integers, R^□_{O,ρ̄,{H_τ},∗} is the reduced, l-torsion-free quotient of the lifting ring whose Q̄_l-points are the lifts that are de Rham with HT_τ = H_τ and have property ∗ ∈ {cris, ss, K′-cris, K′-ss, cr-ord, ss-ord}.
Existence, dimension 1 + n² + [K : Q_l]n(n − 1)/2 and formal smoothness of the generic fibres of the K′-cris rings are Kisin's (LocalGaloisDeformationRings R08.3).
proofSteps: Components: Spec R^□_{K′-cris} is a union of components of Spec R^□_{K″-cris} for K″ ⊇ K′, so "sufficiently large K′" is stable.
Equivalence relation: the generic fibre is formally smooth, so each point lies on a unique component.
Remarks (1), (4)–(7) as in BLGGT p. 26, with (7) proved like Lemma 1.3.5 (a one-parameter family scaling the off-diagonal blocks).
acceptance: Check reflexivity and that ∼ is an equivalence only because the generic fibre is smooth (a point on two components would break transitivity).

nodes.statement: ρ : G_K → GL_n(O_{Q̄_l}) is diagonalizable if it is crystalline and ρ ∼ χ₁ ⊕ ⋯ ⊕ χ_n for crystalline characters χ_i : G_K → O_{Q̄_l}^×; it is potentially diagonalizable if ρ|_{G_{K′}} is diagonalizable for some finite K′/K. By Lemma 1.4.1 potential diagonalizability depends only on the GL_n(Q̄_l)-conjugacy class, so it is defined for ρ : G_K → GL_n(Q̄_l); for a global r with irreducible r̄, "r|_{G_{F_v}} is potentially diagonalizable" refers to the lattice model r°, unique up to conjugation.

nodes.title: Ordinary and Fontaine–Laffaille representations are potentially diagonalizable (Lemma 1.4.3)
nodes.statement: Let ρ : G_K → GL_n(Q̄_l) be potentially crystalline. (1) If ρ has a G_K-invariant filtration with one-dimensional graded pieces (in particular if it is ordinary), then ρ is potentially diagonalizable. (2) If K/Q_l is unramified, ρ is crystalline and HT_τ(ρ) ⊆ [a_τ, a_τ + l − 2] for each τ, then ρ is potentially diagonalizable.

(2): twist to a_τ = 0; ρ̄|_{I_K} has one-dimensional irreducible subquotients, so over an unramified K′ with ρ̄(G_{K′}) = ρ̄(I_K) it has a filtration with one-dimensional pieces; Lemma 1.4.2 lifts that filtered Fontaine–Laffaille module to an l-torsion-free filtered object, giving a crystalline lift ρ₂ with the same Hodge–Tate numbers and a filtration; CHT Lemma 2.4.1 gives ρ|_{G_{K′}} ∼ ρ₂, and (1) applies to ρ₂.

nodes.title: Automorphic polarized representations and their levels
nodes.statement: (r, µ) (resp. (r̄, µ̄), r, r̄) is automorphic if there is a regular algebraic, cuspidal, polarized (π, χ) with (r, µ) ≅ (r_{l,ı}(π), r_{l,ı}(χ)ε_l^{1−n}) (resp. the reductions). It is automorphic of level prime to l, of level potentially prime to l, ordinarily automorphic, or potentially diagonalizably automorphic if some such (π, χ) has level prime to l, has level potentially prime to l, is ı-ordinary, or has level potentially prime to l with r_{l,ı}(π) potentially diagonalizable at all v | l. None of these depends on ı (Clozel, Theorem 3.13).
hypotheses: F is a CM or totally real field with maximal totally real subfield F⁺; l is a prime and ı : Q̄_l ≅ ℂ; for an imaginary CM F, c ∈ Gal(F/F⁺) is complex conjugation and G_n = (GL_n × GL_1) ⋊ {1, j} is the group of BLGGT §1.1 (CHT08).
r_{l,ı}(π) as in blggt-normalization-register (AG2.2).
proofSteps: Definition; independence of ı from Clozel 1990 Theorem 3.13 (algebraic automorphic representations are defined over number fields, cited).
acceptance: Check that (r, µ) automorphic of level prime to l implies potentially diagonalizably automorphic when l is unramified in F and the Hodge–Tate numbers lie in a Fontaine–Laffaille range (potential-diagonalizability-criteria (2)).

nodes.title: Automorphy under twisting and soluble base change (Lemmas 2.2.1–2.2.2)
nodes.statement: (Lemma 2.2.1) For an algebraic character ψ of G_F, with φ = ψ ∘ transfer (F imaginary) or φ = ψ² (F totally real), (r, µ) is automorphic iff (r ⊗ ψ, µφ) is. (Lemma 2.2.2) If M/F is a soluble Galois extension with M CM (or totally real) and (r, µ) is polarized with r|_{G_M} irreducible, then (r, µ) is automorphic iff (r|_{G_M}, µ|_{G_{M⁺}}) is.
hypotheses: F is a CM or totally real field with maximal totally real subfield F⁺; l is a prime and ı : Q̄_l ≅ ℂ; for an imaginary CM F, c ∈ Gal(F/F⁺) is complex conjugation and G_n = (GL_n × GL_1) ⋊ {1, j} is the group of BLGGT §1.1 (CHT08).
proofSteps: 2.2.1: twist π by ψ ∘ det (algebraic Hecke character) and χ by φ.

2.2.2: as CHT Lemma 4.2.2 (and 4.3.2–4.3.3): induct on a cyclic step; base change and descent for GL_n along cyclic extensions (Arthur–Clozel, requested from ET.7a), with irreducibility of r|_{G_M} ensuring cuspidality.

nodes.title: Automorphy of r from automorphy of Ind r (Lemmas 2.2.3–2.2.4)
nodes.statement: (Lemma 2.2.3) An irreducible unitary admissible (gl_n(ℝ) ⊗ ℂ, O(n))- or (gl_n(ℂ) ⊗ ℂ, U(n))-module π with half-integral Harish-Chandra parameter satisfies π^c ≅ π^∨. (Lemma 2.2.4) Let M/F be a soluble Galois CM (or totally real) extension of degree m, r : G_M → GL_n(Q̄_l) irreducible and µ : G_{F⁺} → Q̄_l^× such that (Ind_{G_M}^{G_F} r, µ) is automorphic and polarized. Then (r, µ|_{G_{M⁺}}) is automorphic and polarized.
hypotheses: F is a CM or totally real field with maximal totally real subfield F⁺; l is a prime and ı : Q̄_l ≅ ℂ; for an imaginary CM F, c ∈ Gal(F/F⁺) is complex conjugation and G_n = (GL_n × GL_1) ⋊ {1, j} is the group of BLGGT §1.1 (CHT08).
proofSteps: 2.2.3: the Tadić–Vogan classification writes π as ⊞ of Speh-type blocks built from discrete series σ_i of GL_1(ℝ), GL_2(ℝ) or GL_1(ℂ); each has σ_i^∨ ≅ σ_i^c.

2.2.4: reduce to m prime; Π ⊗ (κ ∘ Art ∘ det) ≅ Π for κ generating Gal(M/F)^∨, so Arthur–Clozel (3.4.2, 3.5.1) and HT Lemma VII.2.6 give BC_{M/F}(Π) = π ⊞ π^σ ⊞ ⋯; the central character and 2.2.3 at ∞ force π^c ≅ π^∨ ⊗ (χ ∘ N ∘ det); compare r_{l,ı}(Π)|_{G_M} with ⊕ r^{σ^j}.

nodes.title: Automorphy lifting: the minimal case (Theorem 2.3.1, after Thorne)
nodes.statement: Let F be imaginary CM, l odd, ζ_l ∉ F and (r, µ) an n-dimensional algebraic polarized l-adic representation of G_F with r̄ irreducible and r̄(G_{F(ζ_l)}) adequate. Suppose (r, µ) ≅ (r_{l,ı}(π), r_{l,ı}(χ)ε_l^{1−n}) residually for a regular algebraic cuspidal polarized (π, χ) of level potentially prime to l with r_{l,ı}(π)|_{G_{F_v}} ∼ r|_{G_{F_v}} at every finite v. Then (r, µ) is automorphic of level potentially prime to l, and of level prime to l if π has level prime to l and r is crystalline above l. (Theorem 2.3.2, Thorne 10.1: the corresponding universal deformation ring R^univ_𝒮 is finite over O_L.)
hypotheses: F is a CM or totally real field with maximal totally real subfield F⁺; l is a prime and ı : Q̄_l ≅ ℂ; for an imaginary CM F, c ∈ Gal(F/F⁺) is complex conjugation and G_n = (GL_n × GL_1) ⋊ {1, j} is the group of BLGGT §1.1 (CHT08).
proofSteps: Thorne Theorem 7.1 (Taylor–Wiles–Kisin patching with adequate image; cited, gap).
For v ∤ l, r_{l,ı}(π)|_{G_{F_v}} ⇝ r|_{G_{F_v}} by Lemma 1.3.2, since ıWD(r_{l,ı}(π)|_{G_{F_v}})^{F-ss} ≅ rec(π_v ⊗ |det|^{(1−n)/2}) and π_v is generic.
acceptance: Check that the hypothesis ∼ at every finite v fixes the components of the local lifting rings: the "minimal" case in the sense of Taylor–Wiles.

sources.match: Theorem 2.3.1 as the output of Taylor–Wiles–Kisin, and Theorem 2.3.2.

nodes.title: Automorphy lifting: the ordinary case (Theorem 2.4.1, after Geraghty and Thorne)
nodes.statement: Let F be CM or totally real, l odd, and (r, µ) an n-dimensional algebraic polarized l-adic representation of G_F with r̄ irreducible, r̄(G_{F(ζ_l)}) adequate, ζ_l ∉ F, r ordinary at every prime above l, and (r̄, µ̄) ordinarily automorphic. Then (r, µ) is ordinarily automorphic, of level prime to l if r is crystalline (potentially prime to l if r is potentially crystalline) above l. (Theorem 2.4.2 = Thorne 10.2: the ss-ordinary universal ring is finite over O_L.)
hypotheses: F is a CM or totally real field with maximal totally real subfield F⁺; l is a prime and ı : Q̄_l ≅ ℂ; for an imaginary CM F, c ∈ Gal(F/F⁺) is complex conjugation and G_n = (GL_n × GL_1) ⋊ {1, j} is the group of BLGGT §1.1 (CHT08).
proofSteps: F imaginary: Thorne Theorem 9.1 (Taylor–Wiles–Kisin with Taylor's level-changing and Hida theory, relaxing the bigness of Geraghty Theorem 5.3.2; cited, gap).
F totally real: base change to an imaginary CM quadratic extension and descend (automorphy-twist-and-soluble-base-change).
acceptance: Check that weights and levels may change: only the residual representation must be ordinarily automorphic.

nodes.title: Moret–Bailly with prescribed local Galois extensions (Proposition 3.1.1)
nodes.statement: Let K^{(avoid)}/K/K₀ be number fields with K^{(avoid)}/K and K/K₀ Galois, S a finite set of places of K₀, and for v ∈ S_K a finite Galois L′_v/K_v with L′_{σv} = σL′_v. Let T/K be smooth and geometrically connected with non-empty Gal(L′_v/K_v)-invariant open Ω_v ⊆ T(L′_v). Then there are a finite Galois L/K and P ∈ T(L) with L/K₀ Galois, L linearly disjoint from K^{(avoid)} over K, and L_w ≅ L′_v with P ∈ Ω_v for w | v ∈ S_K.
hypotheses: Places and extensions as stated.
proofSteps: Enlarge S (Weil bounds and Hensel give K_v-points for almost all v) so that each simple Galois subextension of K^{(avoid)}/K is non-split at some v ∈ S_K with L′_v = K_v; this gives linear disjointness.
Reduce to L′_v = K_v by a soluble extension with prescribed completions (CHT Lemma 4.1.2) and its normal closure over K₀.
Apply Moret-Bailly's Théorème 1.3 and take the normal closure over K₀.
acceptance: Check the role of Ω_v: the point lies in the prescribed open at every place above S, which is what the Dwork-family argument needs at l_i, l′ and ∞.

nodes.title: Potential ordinary automorphy of symplectic mod l representations (Theorem 3.1.2)
nodes.statement: Let F/F₀ be a finite Galois extension of totally real fields, I finite, and for i ∈ I let n_i be even, l_i odd, ı_i : Q̄_{l_i} ≅ ℂ and r̄_i : G_F → GSp_{n_i}(F̄_{l_i}) with open kernel and multiplier ε̄_{l_i}^{1−n_i}; let F^{(avoid)}/F be finite Galois. Then there are a finite totally real F′/F, Galois over F₀ and linearly disjoint from F^{(avoid)}, and regular algebraic cuspidal polarized (π_i, χ_i) of GL_{n_i}(𝔸_{F′}) with (r̄_{l_i,ı_i}(π_i), r̄_{l_i,ı_i}(χ_i)ε̄^{1−n_i}) ≅ (r̄_i|_{G_{F′}}, ε̄^{1−n_i}) and π_i ı_i-ordinary of weight 0.
hypotheses: F totally real; n_i even.
proofSteps: Follow BLGHT11 Theorem 6.3 (the Dwork family T₀ and its covers T_{r̄_i × r̄′_i}; not read, gap), with changes: choose N, cyclic M_i/ℚ of degree n_i, a prime q, characters φ_i, an auxiliary l′ and induced r′_i = Ind θ_i avoiding the ramification of F^{(avoid)}.
Find F′ and points t_i ∈ T₀^{(i)}(F′) with V[λ_i]_{t_i} ≅ r̄_i, V[λ′]_{t_i} ≅ r̄′_i, v(t_i) < 0 above l_i and > 0 above l′, by moret-bailly-galois-control with T = ∏T_{r̄_i × r̄′_i}.
Automorphy of V[λ′] (induced from characters) propagates along the motive to V[λ_i], which is ordinary (Steinberg) at l_i.
acceptance: Check the conclusion's ordinarity: weight 0 with π_{i,v} Steinberg for v | l_i gives ı_i-ordinary (iota-ordinary).

nodes.title: Ordinary lifts with prescribed local behaviour (Proposition 3.2.1)
nodes.statement: Let F be imaginary CM with ζ_l ∉ F, S a finite set of finite places of F⁺ split in F containing those above l, µ : G_{F⁺} → Q̄_l^× crystalline, unramified outside S, µ(c_v) = −1 for v | ∞ (so HT_τ(µ) = {w}), H_τ sets of n distinct integers with H_{τ∘c} = {w − h}, and r̄ : G_{F⁺} → G_n(F̄_l) unramified outside S with ν ∘ r̄ = µ̄ and r̄^{−1}G_n⁰ = G_F; lifts ρ_v of r̄̆|_{G_{F_ṽ}} for v ∈ S, v ∤ l. Assume r̄̆|_{G_{F(ζ_l)}} irreducible, l ≥ 2(d + 1), and ordinary crystalline lifts of r̄̆|_{G_{F_u}} with HT numbers H_τ for u | l. Then r̄ has a lift r : G_{F⁺} → G_n(O_{Q̄_l}) with ν ∘ r = µ, r̆|_{G_{F_u}} ordinary crystalline with HT numbers H_τ for u | l, r̆|_{G_{F_ṽ}} ∼ ρ_v for v ∤ l, and r unramified outside S.
hypotheses: F is a CM or totally real field with maximal totally real subfield F⁺; l is a prime and ı : Q̄_l ≅ ℂ; for an imaginary CM F, c ∈ Gal(F/F⁺) is complex conjugation and G_n = (GL_n × GL_1) ⋊ {1, j} is the group of BLGGT §1.1 (CHT08).
proofSteps: Twist by a character ψ of G_F (Lemma A.2.5: crystalline above l with chosen HT numbers b_τ, unramified at S ∖ {v | l}, wildly ramified at an auxiliary v_q, ψψ^c = ε_l^{1−2n}µ^{−1}) and induce: I_ψ(r̄) : G_{F⁺} → GSp_{2n}(F̄_l) with multiplier ε̄_l^{1−2n}, irreducible on G_{F⁺(ζ_l)} and with adequate image (ghtt-adequacy-criterion).

dwork-potential-ordinary-automorphy makes I_ψ(r̄) ı-ordinarily automorphic over a totally real F₁⁺; after a further soluble F₂⁺, Thorne's finiteness (Theorem 2.4.2, in ordinary-automorphy-lifting) shows the ordinary deformation ring of r̄ over F₃ is finite over O.

Khare–Wintenberger: the global ring with ordinary crystalline conditions at l and the components of ρ_v elsewhere has Krull dimension ≥ 1 (CHT, Proposition 1.5.1) and is finite over the corresponding ring over F₃, so it has a Q̄_l-point.
acceptance: Check the numerology: a totally odd µ and n distinct Hodge–Tate numbers are exactly what makes the lower bound dim R ≥ 1 of CHT hold.

nodes.title: Potential ordinary automorphy of polarized mod l representations (Proposition 3.3.1)
nodes.statement: Let F/F₀ be finite Galois of imaginary CM fields, I finite, and for i ∈ I: l_i odd with ζ_{l_i} ∉ F; µ_i totally odd de Rham (HT {w_i}); r̄_i : G_F → GL_{n_i}(F̄_{l_i}) irreducible with (r̄_i, µ̄_i) totally odd polarized, r̄_i|_{G_{F(ζ_{l_i})}} irreducible and l_i ≥ 2(d_i + 1); sets H_{i,τ} of n_i distinct integers with H_{i,τ∘c} = {w_i − h}; a finite Galois-stable S ⊇ primes above l_i and ramification; lifts ρ_{i,v} (v ∤ l_i) with ρ^c_{i,cv} ≅ µ_iρ^∨_{i,v}; and F^{(avoid)}. Then there are F′/F finite CM, Galois over F₀ and linearly disjoint from F^{(avoid)}, and regular algebraic cuspidal polarized (π_i, χ_i) over F′ with r̄_{l_i,ı_i}(π_i) ≅ r̄_i|_{G_{F′}}, r_{l_i,ı_i}(χ_i)ε^{1−n_i} = µ_i|_{G_{F′⁺}}, π_i unramified above l_i and outside S, ı_i-ordinary, HT_τ(r_{l_i,ı_i}(π_i)) = H_{i,τ|_F}, and r_{l_i,ı_i}(π_i)|_{G_{F′_u}} ∼ ρ_{i,v}|_{G_{F′_u}} for u | v ∈ S, u ∤ l_i.
hypotheses: F is a CM or totally real field with maximal totally real subfield F⁺; l is a prime and ı : Q̄_l ≅ ℂ; for an imaginary CM F, c ∈ Gal(F/F⁺) is complex conjugation and G_n = (GL_n × GL_1) ⋊ {1, j} is the group of BLGGT §1.1 (CHT08).
proofSteps: Combine dwork-potential-ordinary-automorphy (applied to a symplectic induction of r̄_i to the totally real subfield) with ordinary-lifts-with-local-conditions and ordinary-automorphy-lifting over the resulting extension.
acceptance: Check that the output is ı-ordinary with prescribed Hodge–Tate numbers: the input needed by Theorem 4.5.1 to start the potentially diagonalizable lifting.

nodes.title: A preliminary potentially diagonalizable lifting theorem (Proposition 4.1.1)
nodes.statement: Let F be imaginary CM, l odd, ζ_l ∉ F, (r, µ) regular algebraic, irreducible, n-dimensional, polarized with r|_{G_{F_v}} potentially diagonalizable for v | l, r̄|_{G_{F(ζ_l)}} irreducible and l ≥ 2(d + 1). Suppose (r̄, µ̄) is automorphic of level prime to l, from (π, χ) with r_{l,ı}(π)|_{G_{F_v}} potentially diagonalizable for v | l, the set {h + h′ : h ∈ HT_τ(r), h′ ∈ HT_τ(r_{l,ı}(π))} of n² distinct elements for every τ, and r_{l,ı}(π)|_{G_{F_v}} ∼ r|_{G_{F_v}} for v ∤ l. Then (r, µ) is potentially diagonalizably automorphic.
hypotheses: F is a CM or totally real field with maximal totally real subfield F⁺; l is a prime and ı : Q̄_l ≅ ℂ; for an imaginary CM F, c ∈ Gal(F/F⁺) is complex conjugation and G_n = (GL_n × GL_1) ⋊ {1, j} is the group of BLGGT §1.1 (CHT08).
proofSteps: Soluble CM base change (automorphy-twist-and-soluble-base-change) so that F/F⁺ is unramified, the relevant primes split, r and r_{l,ı}(π) are diagonalizable above l and π is unramified there; write r|_{G_{F_u}} ∼ ⊕ψ_i^{(u)} and r_{l,ı}(π)|_{G_{F_u}} ∼ ⊕φ_i^{(u)}.

Choose a cyclic CM M/F of degree n (Corollary A.2.3) and de Rham characters θ, θ′ of G_M with θ̄ = θ̄′, θθ^c = r_{l,ı}(χ)ε_l^{1−n}, θ′θ′^c = µ, Hodge–Tate numbers those of the φ_i resp. ψ_i, and ramification at an auxiliary q (Lemma A.2.5); then Ind θ ∼ ⊕φ_i and Ind θ′ ∼ ⊕ψ_i locally.

Over a soluble F₁: R = (r ⊗ Ind_{G_M}^{G_F}θ)|_{G_{F₁}} and R′ = (r_{l,ı}(π) ⊗ Ind θ′)|_{G_{F₁}} have R̄ ≅ R̄′, are polarized, R has adequate image (ghtt-adequacy-criterion, using l ∤ n), and R ∼ R′ at every place: at l both connect to (⊕ψ_i) ⊗ (⊕φ_j), regular by the n² condition.
R′ is automorphic of level prime to l: automorphic induction of BC(π) ⊗ φ′ (requested from ET.7a); minimal-automorphy-lifting makes R automorphic.
Recover (r, µ) from R = r ⊗ Ind θ by automorphy-descends-from-induction and a twist.
acceptance: Check the n² regularity condition on n = 2: HT(r) = {0, 1}, HT(r_{l,ı}(π)) = {0, 2} give sums {0, 1, 2, 3}, four distinct (suggested file).

nodes.title: Automorphy lifting for potentially diagonalizable representations (Theorem 4.2.1)
nodes.statement: Let F be imaginary CM, l odd, and (r, µ) a regular algebraic, irreducible, n-dimensional polarized representation of G_F with d as above. Suppose r|_{G_{F_v}} is potentially diagonalizable for all v | l; r̄|_{G_{F(ζ_l)}} is irreducible, l ≥ 2(d + 1) and ζ_l ∉ F; and (r̄, µ̄) is ordinarily automorphic or potentially diagonalizably automorphic. Then (r, µ) is potentially diagonalizably automorphic (of level potentially prime to l). Condition (1) holds in the Fontaine–Laffaille case: l unramified in F, r crystalline above l with HT_τ(r) in some [a_τ, a_τ + l − 2].
hypotheses: F is a CM or totally real field with maximal totally real subfield F⁺; l is a prime and ı : Q̄_l ≅ ℂ; for an imaginary CM F, c ∈ Gal(F/F⁺) is complex conjugation and G_n = (GL_n × GL_1) ⋊ {1, j} is the group of BLGGT §1.1 (CHT08).
proofSteps: After a soluble CM base change linearly disjoint from F̄^{ker r̄}(ζ_l) (automorphy-twist-and-soluble-base-change): F/F⁺ unramified, primes above l and ramification split over F⁺, ζ_l ∈ F_u and r̄, r̄_{l,ı}(π) trivial on G_{F_u} for u | l.

Choose m larger than all differences of Hodge–Tate numbers of r and r_{l,ı}(π), H_τ = {0, m, …, (n − 1)m}; ordinary-lifts-with-local-conditions gives r₁ (level of r, ordinary crystalline with HT H_τ) and, in the second case, r₂ (level of r_{l,ı}(π)).
Ordinary case: ordinary-automorphy-lifting makes r₁ automorphic of level prime to l; preliminary-pd-automorphy-lifting gives r.
PD case: preliminary-pd-automorphy-lifting makes r₂ automorphic; r₂ ordinary of level potentially prime to l makes it ordinarily automorphic (iota-ordinary); reduce to the first case.
acceptance: Check the Fontaine–Laffaille remark against potential-diagonalizability-criteria (2).
Check that neither weight nor level of r need match π: the "change of weight" of the title.

nodes.title: Lifts with potentially diagonalizable local conditions (Theorem 4.3.1)
nodes.statement: In the setting of §4.3 (F imaginary CM with ζ_l ∉ F, S split containing places above l, µ algebraic unramified outside S with µ(c_v) = −1, r̄ : G_{F⁺} → G_n(F̄_l) unramified outside S with ν ∘ r̄ = µ̄, lifts ρ_v of r̄̆|_{G_{F_ṽ}} for v ∈ S), assume r̄̆|_{G_{F(ζ_l)}} irreducible, l ≥ 2(d + 1), and for v | l that ρ_v is potentially diagonalizable with n distinct τ-Hodge–Tate numbers. Then r̄ has a lift r : G_{F⁺} → G_n(O_{Q̄_l}) with ν ∘ r = µ, r̆|_{G_{F_ṽ}} ∼ ρ_v for v ∈ S, unramified outside S.
hypotheses: F is a CM or totally real field with maximal totally real subfield F⁺; l is a prime and ı : Q̄_l ≅ ℂ; for an imaginary CM F, c ∈ Gal(F/F⁺) is complex conjugation and G_n = (GL_n × GL_1) ⋊ {1, j} is the group of BLGGT §1.1 (CHT08).
proofSteps: As in Theorem 4.2.1: the deformation ring with the components of the ρ_v has dimension ≥ 1; potential automorphy of r̄ (potential-ordinary-automorphy) and pd-automorphy-lifting over the extension make it finite over O; so it has Q̄_l-points.
acceptance: Check that this strengthens ordinary-lifts-with-local-conditions: ordinary crystalline ρ_v are potentially diagonalizable.

nodes.title: Change of weight and level (Theorem 4.4.1)
nodes.statement: Let F be imaginary CM, l > 2(n + 1) with ζ_l ∉ F and primes above l split over F⁺, S a finite split set of finite places of F⁺ containing those above l, µ algebraic, and r̄ : G_F → GL_n(F̄_l) with (r̄, µ̄) polarized, unramified outside S, ordinarily or potentially diagonalizably automorphic, and r̄|_{G_{F(ζ_l)}} irreducible. For v ∈ S let ρ_v be a lift of r̄|_{G_{F_ṽ}}, potentially diagonalizable with n distinct τ-Hodge–Tate numbers when v | l. Then there is a regular algebraic cuspidal polarized (π, χ) with r̄_{l,ı}(π) ≅ r̄, r_{l,ı}(χ)ε_l^{1−n} = µ, level potentially prime to l, unramified outside S, and ρ_v ∼ r_{l,ı}(π)|_{G_{F_ṽ}} for v ∈ S.
hypotheses: F is a CM or totally real field with maximal totally real subfield F⁺; l is a prime and ı : Q̄_l ≅ ℂ; for an imaginary CM F, c ∈ Gal(F/F⁺) is complex conjugation and G_n = (GL_n × GL_1) ⋊ {1, j} is the group of BLGGT §1.1 (CHT08).
The statement is read with ρ_v a lift of r̄|_{G_{F_ṽ}}; see ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions/E3.
proofSteps: pd-lifts-with-local-conditions gives a lift r with the local conditions ρ_v; pd-automorphy-lifting makes it automorphic; local–global compatibility (blggt-normalization-register (3)) gives ρ_v ∼ r_{l,ı}(π)|_{G_{F_ṽ}}.
acceptance: Check the Serre-weight reading: r̄ is automorphic in every potentially diagonalizable weight and type it admits locally.

nodes.title: Potential automorphy of potentially diagonalizable polarized representations (Theorem 4.5.1)
nodes.statement: Let F/F₀ be finite Galois of imaginary CM fields, I finite, and for i ∈ I: n_i, d_i ≥ 1, l_i odd with l_i ≥ 2(d_i + 1) and ζ_{l_i} ∉ F, ı_i; (r_i, µ_i) a totally odd, regular algebraic, n_i-dimensional polarized l_i-adic representation of G_F with d_i the maximal dimension of an irreducible constituent of r̄_i restricted to the subgroup generated by the Sylow pro-l_i-subgroups; F^{(avoid)}/F finite Galois. Assume r_i is potentially diagonalizable at each prime of F above l_i and r̄_i|_{G_{F(ζ_{l_i})}} is irreducible. Then there are a finite CM F′/F, Galois over F₀ and linearly disjoint from F^{(avoid)} over F, and regular algebraic cuspidal polarized (π_i, χ_i) of GL_{n_i}(𝔸_{F′}), unramified above l_i, with (r_{l_i,ı_i}(π_i), r_{l_i,ı_i}(χ_i)ε_{l_i}^{1−n_i}) ≅ (r_i|_{G_{F′}}, µ_i|_{G_{(F′)⁺}}).
hypotheses: F is a CM or totally real field with maximal totally real subfield F⁺; l is a prime and ı : Q̄_l ≅ ℂ; for an imaginary CM F, c ∈ Gal(F/F⁺) is complex conjugation and G_n = (GL_n × GL_1) ⋊ {1, j} is the group of BLGGT §1.1 (CHT08).
Read "each prime v of F above l_i" (the printed "of F⁺" is a misprint, ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions/E2).
proofSteps: potential-ordinary-automorphy gives F′ (Galois over F₀, disjoint from ∩ ker r̄_i · F^{(avoid)}(ζ_{∏l_i})) and ı_i-ordinary (π′_i, χ′_i) with r̄_{l_i,ı_i}(π′_i) ≅ r̄_i|_{G_{F′}}, unramified above l_i.
pd-automorphy-lifting over F′ (hypotheses preserved: potential diagonalizability restricts, and r̄_i|_{G_{F′(ζ_{l_i})}} stays irreducible by disjointness).
acceptance: Check the Fontaine–Laffaille special case: l_i unramified in F⁺, r_i crystalline above l_i with HT in [a_τ, a_τ + l − 2] (potential-diagonalizability-criteria (2)).
Check that the output is automorphy over F′ only: descent to F needs automorphy-twist-and-soluble-base-change and holds only for soluble F′/F.

nodes.title: Potential automorphy over totally real fields (Corollary 4.5.2)
nodes.statement: Let F⁺ be totally real, l ≥ 2(n + 1), and (r, µ) a totally odd, regular algebraic, n-dimensional polarized l-adic representation of G_{F⁺}, potentially diagonalizable at each prime above l, with r̄|_{G_{F⁺(ζ_l)}} irreducible. Then there is a Galois totally real F^{+,′}/F⁺ such that (r|_{G_{F^{+,′}}}, µ|_{G_{F^{+,′}}}) is automorphic of level prime to l.
hypotheses: F⁺ totally real.
proofSteps: Choose an imaginary quadratic F/F⁺ in which primes above l split, disjoint from (F̄⁺)^{ker ad r̄}(ζ_l); apply potential-automorphy-theorem to r|_{G_F}; descend from the CM field F′ to (F′)⁺ by automorphy-twist-and-soluble-base-change.
acceptance: Check against KW/Taylor over ℚ: for n = 2 this recovers potential modularity of odd regular 2-dimensional representations with PD local conditions.

nodes.title: Potential automorphy of mod l representations with prescribed local lifts (Corollary 4.5.3)
nodes.statement: In the situation of Theorem 4.5.1 but with r̄_i : G_F → GL_{n_i}(F̄_{l_i}) irreducible, (r̄_i, µ_i) polarized (µ_i totally odd de Rham), r̄_i|_{G_{F(ζ_{l_i})}} irreducible, S a Gal(F/F⁺)-stable finite set of primes containing those above l_i and the ramification, and lifts ρ_{i,v} (v ∈ S) with ρ^c_{i,cv} ≅ µ_iρ^∨_{i,v}, potentially diagonalizable with n_i distinct Hodge–Tate numbers when v | l_i: there are F′ (as in 4.5.1) and (π_i, χ_i) with r̄_{l_i,ı_i}(π_i) ≅ r̄_i|_{G_{F′}}, r_{l_i,ı_i}(χ_i)ε^{1−n_i} = µ_i|_{G_{F′⁺}}, level potentially prime to l_i, unramified outside S, and r_{l_i,ı_i}(π_i)|_{G_{F′_u}} ∼ ρ_{i,v}|_{G_{F′_u}} for u | v ∈ S.
hypotheses: F is a CM or totally real field with maximal totally real subfield F⁺; l is a prime and ı : Q̄_l ≅ ℂ; for an imaginary CM F, c ∈ Gal(F/F⁺) is complex conjugation and G_n = (GL_n × GL_1) ⋊ {1, j} is the group of BLGGT §1.1 (CHT08).
Read ρ_{i,v}, n_i and ρ_{i,v}|_{G_{F′_u}} in (g) and (7) (misprints E2).
proofSteps: Reduce to S split over F⁺ as in potential-ordinary-automorphy; pd-lifts-with-local-conditions gives lifts r_i with r_i|_{G_{F_v}} ∼ ρ_{i,v}; apply potential-automorphy-theorem.
acceptance: Check that it strengthens Proposition 3.3.1: the local conditions may be any potentially diagonalizable types, not only ordinary.

nodes.title: Potential automorphy of compatible systems (Theorem 5.4.1, Corollary 5.4.2)
nodes.statement: Let F/F₀ be finite Galois of CM (resp. totally real) fields and F^{(avoid)}/F finite Galois. If (ℛ_i, ℳ_i), i = 1, …, r, are totally odd, polarized weakly compatible systems of l-adic representations of G_F with each ℛ_i regular and irreducible, then there is a finite CM (resp. totally real) F′/F, linearly disjoint from F^{(avoid)} and Galois over F₀, such that each (ℛ_i|_{G_{F′}}, ℳ_i|_{G_{(F′)⁺}}) is automorphic. In particular (Corollary 5.4.2) a single such system becomes automorphic over a finite Galois CM (resp. totally real) F′/F.
hypotheses: (ℛ, ℳ) a polarized weakly compatible system of G_F over M (PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems R24.5: members (r_λ, µ_λ) polarized); BLGGT v4 §5.1 conventions.
proofSteps: Totally real case from the CM case by automorphy-twist-and-soluble-base-change, choosing F′ disjoint from the fields F_i¹ of Lemma 5.3.1 (rank-two-reducibility-independent-of-lambda) so that ℛ_i stays irreducible (Lemma A.2.1).
Take M common; L = ∩_i(L_{i,1} ∩ L_{i,2}) of density 1, with L_{i,1} from residual-irreducibility-density-one and L_{i,2} the primes where ℛ_i is irreducible (Lemma A.1.7).
Remove finitely many l: l ≥ 2(dim ℛ_i + 1), l unramified in F and not below the bad primes, Hodge–Tate numbers in some [a, a + l − 2].
potential-diagonalizability-criteria (2) makes r_{i,λ} potentially diagonalizable; apply potential-automorphy-theorem to the r_{i,λ} for one λ | l ∈ L.
acceptance: Check the density-one bookkeeping: the intersection of finitely many density-one sets has density one.
Check the Fontaine–Laffaille step: for l large the Hodge–Tate range (fixed by the system) has length < l − 2.

sources.locator: §5.4, Theorem 5.4.1, Corollary 5.4.2 and proof, p. 74 (arXiv v4)
sources.match: Theorem 5.4.1 (v1 Theorem 5.3.1), Corollary 5.4.2 and the proof.

nodes.title: Meromorphic continuation, functional equation and purity for compatible systems (Corollary 5.4.3)
nodes.statement: Under the hypotheses of Corollary 5.4.2: (1) for ı : M ↪ ℂ, L^S(ıℛ, s) converges uniformly absolutely on compact subsets of a right half plane and continues meromorphically to ℂ; (2) ℛ is strictly pure and Λ(ıℛ, s) = ε(ıℛ, s)Λ(ıℛ^∨, 1 − s); (3) if F is totally real, n is odd and v | ∞, then tr r_λ(c_v) = ±1 is independent of λ.
hypotheses: (ℛ, ℳ) a polarized weakly compatible system of G_F over M (PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems R24.5: members (r_λ, µ_λ) polarized); BLGGT v4 §5.1 conventions.
proofSteps: Strict purity: Theorem 5.4.1, Theorem 2.1.1 (purity of WD at v ∤ l for automorphic members) and Brauer's theorem as in the proof of part-of-compatible-system (the Grothendieck-ring argument of PM R24.5/galois-grothendieck-ring).

Continuation and functional equation: over each soluble F′/F_i in a Brauer decomposition 1 = Σ n_i Ind ψ_i the system is automorphic, so L^S(ıℛ, s) = ∏ L^S(π_i ⊗ ψ_i, s)^{n_i} (HSBT10 Theorem 4.2 argument), each factor entire with the standard functional equation (AL.2).
(3): reduce to the automorphic case, Taylor 2012 (the Calegari observation); cited.
acceptance: Check that the Γ- and ε-factors are those of PM R24.5/system-l-functions, so (2) is the functional equation that node could not claim.
Check the example of an elliptic curve over a totally real field: L(E, s) continues and satisfies its functional equation (the system is regular, irreducible, polarized).

nodes.title: Tensor products of non-CM modular forms (Corollary 5.4.4)
nodes.statement: Let K ⊆ ℤ_{>0} be finite with the 2^{#K} partial sums of its elements distinct, and f_k (k ∈ K) non-CM newforms of weight k + 1 with automorphic π_k. Then there are a totally real Galois F/ℚ and a regular algebraic polarizable cuspidal Π on GL_{2^{#K}}(𝔸_F) with rec(Π_v|det|^{(1−2^{#K})/2}) = (⊗_k rec(π_{k,v|ℚ}|det|^{−1/2}))|_{W_{F_v}} for almost all v; in particular L(×_k π_k, s) continues meromorphically to ℂ.
hypotheses: f_k non-CM; the partial-sum condition gives regularity of ⊗_k r_{k,λ}.
proofSteps: Apply compatible-systems-potentially-automorphic to ⊗_K r_{k,λ}.

Irreducibility (Goursat): the Zariski closure H̄ of (∏ r_{k,λ})(G_ℚ) in PGL_2^K surjects onto each factor; as PGL_2 is simple with only inner automorphisms, H̄ = PGL_2^I with K = ⊔ K_i mapping diagonally; #K_i > 1 would give r_{k,λ} ≅ r_{k′,λ} ⊗ χ with χ de Rham, contradicting Hodge–Tate numbers; so H ⊇ SL_2^K, whose tensor representation is irreducible.
acceptance: Check the partial-sum condition on K = {1, 2, 4}: the 8 subset sums 0, …, 7 are distinct; on K = {1, 2, 3} they are not (1 + 2 = 3) (suggested file).

nodes.title: Constituents of polarized systems are potentially automorphic (Proposition 5.4.6)
nodes.statement: Let F be CM and (ℛ, ℳ) a totally odd, polarized weakly compatible system with ℛ pure and extremely regular; write r_λ = r_{λ,1} ⊕ ⋯ ⊕ r_{λ,j_λ} into irreducibles. There is a set L of rational primes of Dirichlet density 1 such that for λ | l ∈ L there is a finite CM Galois F′/F with each (r_{λ,α}|_{G_{F′}}, µ_λ|_{G_{(F′)⁺}}) irreducible and automorphic.
hypotheses: (ℛ, ℳ) a polarized weakly compatible system of G_F over M (PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems R24.5: members (r_λ, µ_λ) polarized); BLGGT v4 §5.1 conventions.
proofSteps: Lemma 5.4.5 (PM R24.5/constituents-essentially-self-dual, v1 Lemma 5.2.3): each (r_{λ,α}, µ_λ) is totally odd polarized.

L from residual-irreducibility-density-one, minus finitely many l (l ≥ 2(dim ℛ + 1), unramified, Fontaine–Laffaille range); potential-diagonalizability-criteria (2); potential-automorphy-theorem with F^{(avoid)} the compositum of the F̄^{ker r̄_{λ,α}}.
acceptance: Check that irreducibility over F′ comes from the choice of F^{(avoid)}: r̄_{λ,α}|_{G_{F′}} stays irreducible, hence so does r_{λ,α}|_{G_{F′}}.

nodes.title: A potentially diagonalizable polarized representation lies in a compatible system (Theorem 5.5.1)
nodes.statement: Let F be CM, l ≥ 2(n + 1) with ζ_l ∉ F, and (r, µ) an n-dimensional totally odd regular algebraic polarized l-adic representation of G_F, potentially diagonalizable above l with r̄|_{G_{F(ζ_l)}} irreducible. Then r is part of a strictly pure compatible system of l-adic representations of G_F.
hypotheses: F is a CM or totally real field with maximal totally real subfield F⁺; l is a prime and ı : Q̄_l ≅ ℂ; for an imaginary CM F, c ∈ Gal(F/F⁺) is complex conjugation and G_n = (GL_n × GL_1) ⋊ {1, j} is the group of BLGGT §1.1 (CHT08).
proofSteps: potential-automorphy-theorem gives F′/F Galois CM, disjoint from F⁰F̄^{ker r̄} (F⁰ cut out by the component group of the Zariski closure of r), and (π, χ) over F′ with r_{l,ı}(π) = r|_{G_{F′}}; soluble descent gives π(F″) for F′/F″ soluble.
For each (l′, ı′), decompose r_{l′,ı′}(π) into irreducibles; the component groups are independent of l′ (Lemma 5.3.1), so the pieces descend to each F″.

Brauer: 1 = Σ n_i Ind_{F′_i}ψ_i with F′/F′_i soluble; set A_{l′,ı′,α} = Σ n_i ind_{F′_i/F}([r_{l′,ı′}(π(F′_i))_α][ı′^{−1}ψ_i]) in Rep_{F,l′}; dim A = dim r_{l′,ı′}(π)_α and (A, A) = 1, so A = [r_{l′,ı′,α}] is a genuine irreducible representation (PM R24.5/galois-grothendieck-ring).
r_{l′,ı′} = ⊕_α r_{l′,ı′,α} has r_{l,ı} ≅ r; its Weil–Deligne representations are pure (Theorem 2.1.1, Lemma 1.3.6) and have l′-independent traces, so the system is strictly pure and compatible.
acceptance: Check the Grothendieck-ring step: (A, A) = 1 with dim A ≥ 0 is exactly the criterion recorded in PM R24.5/galois-grothendieck-ring (4).

sources.match: Theorem 5.5.1 (v1 Theorem 5.4.1) and its Brauer-induction proof.

nodes.title: Irreducibility of r_{l,ı}(π) for density-one l (Theorem 5.5.2)
nodes.statement: Let F be CM and π a regular algebraic, polarizable, cuspidal automorphic representation of GL_n(𝔸_F) of extremely regular weight. Then there is a set L of rational primes of Dirichlet density 1 such that r_{l,ı}(π) is irreducible for every l ∈ L and ı : Q̄_l ≅ ℂ.
hypotheses: F is a CM or totally real field with maximal totally real subfield F⁺; l is a prime and ı : Q̄_l ≅ ℂ; for an imaginary CM F, c ∈ Gal(F/F⁺) is complex conjugation and G_n = (GL_n × GL_1) ⋊ {1, j} is the group of BLGGT §1.1 (CHT08).
proofSteps: Apply constituents-potentially-automorphic to ℛ = {r_{l,ı}(π)}; for l ∈ L write r_{l,ı}(π) = ⊕_{α=1}^j r_{l,ı}(π)_α, each potentially automorphic.
ord_{s=1}L^S(ı(ℛ ⊗ ℛ^∨), s) = ord_{s=1}L^S(π × π^∨, s) = −1 (Jacquet–Shalika, Shahidi; requested from AL.3).
On the other hand, using the potential automorphy of the constituents and Brauer induction, the order is −j; hence j = 1.
acceptance: Check the Rankin–Selberg input: L^S(π × π′^∨, s) has a simple pole at s = 1 exactly when π′ is a twist of π, and is holomorphic nonvanishing there otherwise.

nodes.title: Splitting a polarized system into irreducible systems (Theorem 5.5.3)
nodes.statement: Let F be CM and ℛ a pure, extremely regular, totally odd, polarizable weakly compatible system of G_F. Then ℛ = ℛ_1 ⊕ ⋯ ⊕ ℛ_s with each ℛ_i an irreducible, strictly pure, totally odd, polarizable compatible system.
hypotheses: (ℛ, ℳ) a polarized weakly compatible system of G_F over M (PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems R24.5: members (r_λ, µ_λ) polarized); BLGGT v4 §5.1 conventions.
proofSteps: Choose L of density 1 for residual-irreducibility-density-one and constituents-potentially-automorphic; pick λ | l ∈ L with l ≥ 2(n + 1), unramified, Fontaine–Laffaille Hodge–Tate range; decompose r_λ = ⊕ r_{λ,α}.

part-of-compatible-system puts each r_{λ,α} in a strictly pure compatible system ℛ_α; over F′ it is the system of an extremely regular π_α, so irreducibility-density-one makes ℛ_α irreducible on a density-one set.
Compare Frobenius polynomials: ⊕ℛ_α and ℛ agree at r_λ, hence everywhere.
acceptance: Check the degenerate case s = 1: an irreducible system is its own decomposition, with the added conclusion of strict purity.

nodes.title: The symmetric power lifting Sym^{n−1}π
nodes.statement: For π cuspidal on GL₂(𝔸_ℚ) and n ≥ 1, a symmetric power lifting Sym^{n−1}π is an automorphic representation Π of GL_n(𝔸_ℚ) with rec(Π_v) ≅ Sym^{n−1} ∘ rec(π_v) for every place v (local Langlands for GL₂ and GL_n). For π regular algebraic and non-CM, Sym^{n−1}π exists as a regular algebraic cuspidal representation iff Sym^{n−1}r_{π,ι} is automorphic in the sense of ML.2/automorphic-galois-representation for one (equivalently every) p and ι : Q̄_p ≅ ℂ (strong multiplicity one, Chebotarev density and local–global compatibility); for CM π or weight-one π the lifting is isobaric and usually not cuspidal.
hypotheses: π a cuspidal automorphic representation of GL₂(𝔸_ℚ), regular algebraic (from a holomorphic newform of weight k ≥ 2) unless said otherwise; r_{π,ι} : G_ℚ → GL₂(Q̄_p) its Galois representation (Tate-normalised: WD(r_{π,ι}|_{G_{ℚ_l}})^{F-ss} ≅ rec^T(ι^{−1}π_l)); n ≥ 2.
proofSteps: Galois criterion: an automorphic Π with r_{Π,ι} ≅ Sym^{n−1}r_{π,ι} has the right Satake parameters at almost all l, and local–global compatibility at the remaining l gives rec(Π_l) = Sym^{n−1}rec(π_l).
Cuspidality for non-CM π: Sym^{n−1}r_{π,ι} is irreducible because the Zariski closure of r_{π,ι}(G_ℚ) contains SL₂ (Ribet).
acceptance: Check the known small cases: n = 2 is π itself; n = 3 is Gelbart–Jacquet; n = 4, 5 are Kim–Shahidi (cited in Newton–Thorne's introduction).

nodes.title: Accessible and n-regular refinements
nodes.statement: For a definite unitary group G_n over F⁺ and an automorphic π of G_n(𝔸_{F⁺}) with p-adic places S_p, an accessible refinement is a choice χ = (χ_v)_{v∈S_p} of smooth characters χ_v : T_n(F_ṽ) → Q̄_p^× occurring as subquotients of the normalised Jacquet module ι^{−1}r_{N_n}(π_v), equivalently with π_v ↪ i^{GL_n}_{B_n}ιχ_v. For n = 2 it is n-regular if (χ_{v,1}/χ_{v,2})^i ≠ 1 for 1 ≤ i ≤ n − 1 and every v ∈ S_p. For π on GL₂(𝔸_ℚ), π_l has an accessible refinement iff its Jacquet module is nonzero, iff π_l is not supercuspidal.
hypotheses: G_n the definite unitary group of NT §1; T_n ⊂ B_n ⊂ GL_n diagonal torus and upper Borel.
proofSteps: Definition; the equivalence with non-supercuspidality: an irreducible π_l embeds into a principal series iff its Jacquet module is nonzero.
acceptance: Check that an n-regular refinement excludes the ratio being an i-th root of unity for i < n: the condition keeps Sym^{n−1} of the refinement regular.

nodes.title: Automorphy of Sym^{n−1} is constant on eigencurve components (NT I Theorem 2.33)
nodes.statement: Let (π₀, χ₀), (π′₀, χ′₀) be refined points of the eigencurve E₀ (tame level N, prime p) with corresponding points z₀, z′₀. Suppose either (1) χ₀ is numerically non-critical and n-regular, (2) χ′₀ is n-regular, (3) the Zariski closures of r_{π₀,ι}(G_{ℚ_p}) and r_{π′₀,ι}(G_{ℚ_p}) contain SL₂, (4) Sym^{n−1}r_{π₀,ι} is automorphic; or (1ord) χ₀ is ordinary, (2ord) π₀, π′₀ are not CM, (3ord) Sym^{n−1}r_{π₀,ι} is automorphic. If z₀, z′₀ lie on a common irreducible component of E_{0,ℂ_p}, then Sym^{n−1}r_{π′₀,ι} is automorphic.
hypotheses: π a cuspidal automorphic representation of GL₂(𝔸_ℚ), regular algebraic (from a holomorphic newform of weight k ≥ 2) unless said otherwise; r_{π,ι} : G_ℚ → GL₂(Q̄_p) its Galois representation (Tate-normalised: WD(r_{π,ι}|_{G_{ℚ_l}})^{F-ss} ≅ rec^T(ι^{−1}π_l)); n ≥ 2.
E₀ the Coleman–Mazur eigencurve and E_n the eigenvariety of a definite unitary group in n variables (PadicFamilies L2).
proofSteps: Transfer to definite unitary groups G₂ and G_n over a CM field (Theorem 2.24): the map σ_n ∘ i₂ sends E₂ into E_n near z₂ when an infinitesimal R = T holds.
The R = T theorem follows from vanishing of the adjoint Bloch–Kato Selmer group of Sym^{n−1} (Newton–Thorne 2020, cited; Kisin and Bellaïche–Chenevier's method).
Irreducible components: the locus where the image lies in E_n is Zariski closed and contains a neighbourhood of z₂, hence the component.
acceptance: Check the ordinary variant: an ordinary refinement is automatically numerically non-critical, and Hida families replace eigencurve components.

nodes.title: The tame-level-one 2-adic eigencurve near the boundary (Buzzard–Kilford)
nodes.statement: For p = 2 and N = 1, E₀ lies over the component W₀⁺ (χ(−1) = 1) of weight space, and w = χ_u(5) − 1 identifies W₀⁺ with {|w| < 1}. Over the annulus W₀(b) = {|8| < |w| < 1}, E₀(b) = κ^{−1}(W₀(b)) is a disjoint union ⊔_{i≥1}X_i of admissible opens with κ|_{X_i} an isomorphism onto W₀(b), and on X_i the slope is i·v₂(w).
hypotheses: p = 2, tame level 1.
proofSteps: Buzzard–Kilford 2005 (explicit overconvergence of U₂ in the boundary region; cited, not read).
acceptance: Check the consequence used: every irreducible component of E₀ meets κ^{−1}(W₀(b)), so it contains some X_i.

nodes.title: Symmetric powers for one level-one form give them for all (NT I Theorem 3.1 = Theorem D)
nodes.statement: Fix n ≥ 2. If π₀ is an everywhere unramified cuspidal π of weight k ≥ 2 with Sym^{n−1}r_{π₀,ι} automorphic for some (equivalently any) p and ι, then Sym^{n−1}r_{π,ι} is automorphic for every everywhere unramified cuspidal π of weight ≥ 2.
hypotheses: π a cuspidal automorphic representation of GL₂(𝔸_ℚ), regular algebraic (from a holomorphic newform of weight k ≥ 2) unless said otherwise; r_{π,ι} : G_ℚ → GL₂(Q̄_p) its Galois representation (Tate-normalised: WD(r_{π,ι}|_{G_{ℚ_l}})^{F-ss} ≅ rec^T(ι^{−1}π_l)); n ≥ 2.
proofSteps: Work on the 2-adic tame-level-1 eigencurve E₀ (all points share the trivial residual representation).
By eigenvariety-propagation, automorphy of Sym^{n−1} is constant on components; each component contains some annulus X_i (buzzard-kilford-eigencurve).

Ping pong: a level-one f of weight k gives the two points (f, α), (f, β) on X_i, X_{i′} with i + i′ = (k − 1)/v₂(w(κ)); alternating swaps (f′, α′) ↔ (f′, β′) with moves inside annuli reach every X_i from a well-chosen starting point (classical points ramified at 2 are used to reach the boundary annulus).
acceptance: Check the key numerical identity v₂(α) + v₂(β) = k − 1 for the two roots of X² − a₂X + 2^{k−1}, which gives i + i′ = (k − 1)/v₂(w).

sources.match: Theorem 3.1 (Theorem D) and the ping-pong strategy.

nodes.title: Finiteness of ordinary deformation rings with reducible residual image (NT I Theorem 5.2)
nodes.statement: In the setting of NT I §5 (a residually reducible r̄ = ⊕χ_i of G_F for F CM, ordinary deformation problems 𝒮_Σ with Σ a set of auxiliary places), suppose (1) p > 2n, (2) χ_i/χ_j|_{G_{F(ζ_p)}} has order > 2n for i < j (so r̄ is Schur), (3) [F(ζ_p) : F] = p − 1 and (4) Σ ≠ ∅. Then R_{𝒮_Σ} is a finite Λ-algebra.
hypotheses: The notation and hypotheses of NT I §5.
proofSteps: Controls the dimension of the locus of reducible deformations (used in §6 to find a generic prime of the ordinary Hecke algebra); proof in NT I §5 not decomposed here.
acceptance: Check the role: finiteness gives the dimension bound needed to find a non-reducible point, not an R = T theorem.

nodes.title: Level raising to Steinberg for symmetric powers of theta series (NT I Theorems 4.1, 6.1, 7.1)
nodes.statement: Let n ≥ 3, p ≡ 1 (mod 48·n!), q ≠ p, X₀ a finite set of places of K prime to 2pq and ω a de Rham character with ωω^c = ε³, unramified on X₀. Then there is a soluble CM F/K, X₀-split, and a RACSDC ι-ordinary Π on GL_n(𝔸_F) with r_{Π,ι} ≅ ω^{n−1}|_{G_F} ⊗ Sym^{n−1}r_{σ₀,ι}|_{G_F}, the same Hodge–Tate numbers, and Π_v an unramified twist of Steinberg at some v | q (Theorem 7.1; proved here for n odd, Proposition 7.4; for n even via Anastassiades–Thorne).
hypotheses: σ₀ a theta series congruent to the chosen level-one form (NT I §7); K an imaginary quadratic field.
proofSteps: Theorem 4.1: automorphic level raising with depth-zero types for unitary groups (for n = 3: the cuspidal unipotent representation of U₃(q) stays irreducible mod p when q is a primitive 6th root of unity mod p, Proposition 1.15).
Theorem 6.1: a Steinberg local component via the "R_p = T_p" theorem of Allen–Newton–Thorne for residually reducible representations, using reducible-deformation-finiteness.
Proposition 7.4 assembles these for odd n; Anastassiades–Thorne 2021 passes from Sym^{n−1} to Sym^{2n−1} (cited).
acceptance: Check the arithmetic condition p ≡ 1 (mod 48·n!) on a small case: for n = 3, 48·3! = 288 and p = 577 is a prime ≡ 1 (mod 288) (suggested file).

sources.locator: §7, Theorem 7.1, p. 82; §4 Theorem 4.1, p. 59; §6 Theorem 6.1, p. 75 (arXiv v3)

nodes.title: One level-one form with automorphic Sym^{n−1} (NT I Theorem 7.6 = Theorem E)
nodes.statement: For every n ≥ 3 there is a cuspidal, everywhere unramified π of GL₂(𝔸_ℚ) of weight k ≥ 2 such that Sym^{n−1}r_{π,ι} is automorphic for every ι.
hypotheses: π a cuspidal automorphic representation of GL₂(𝔸_ℚ), regular algebraic (from a holomorphic newform of weight k ≥ 2) unless said otherwise; r_{π,ι} : G_ℚ → GL₂(Q̄_p) its Galois representation (Tate-normalised: WD(r_{π,ι}|_{G_{ℚ_l}})^{F-ss} ≅ rec^T(ι^{−1}π_l)); n ≥ 2.
proofSteps: Choose a level-one form f congruent mod p to a theta series (r̄_{f,ι} ≅ Ind_{G_K}^{G_ℚ}ψ̄), so Sym^{n−1}r̄ restricted to G_K is a sum of characters, residually automorphic by the endoscopic classification (ML.4).

steinberg-level-raising provides a residually matching automorphic Π with a Steinberg component; the Allen–Newton–Thorne / Thorne automorphy lifting theorem for residually reducible representations (requiring a Steinberg component) makes Sym^{n−1}r_{f,ι}|_{G_F} automorphic; soluble descent.
acceptance: Check that the strategy uses small residual image and large p, in contrast to Clozel–Thorne's large image and small p.

sources.match: Theorem 7.6 (Theorem E) and the theta-series strategy.

nodes.title: Symmetric power functoriality in level one (NT I Theorem 7.7 = Theorem A)
nodes.statement: For every n ≥ 2 and every regular algebraic cuspidal automorphic representation π of GL₂(𝔸_ℚ) of level 1, Sym^{n−1}π exists as a regular algebraic cuspidal automorphic representation of GL_n(𝔸_ℚ).
hypotheses: π a cuspidal automorphic representation of GL₂(𝔸_ℚ), regular algebraic (from a holomorphic newform of weight k ≥ 2) unless said otherwise; r_{π,ι} : G_ℚ → GL₂(Q̄_p) its Galois representation (Tate-normalised: WD(r_{π,ι}|_{G_{ℚ_l}})^{F-ss} ≅ rec^T(ι^{−1}π_l)); n ≥ 2.
π everywhere unramified.
proofSteps: n = 2 is trivial; for n ≥ 3 combine one-level-one-symmetric-power with level-one-ping-pong, then symmetric-power-lifting (Galois criterion).
acceptance: Check on Δ (weight 12, level 1): Sym^{n−1}Δ exists for every n, so L(Sym^{n−1}Δ, s) is entire.

nodes.title: Congruences to n-regular forms (NT I Proposition 8.3)
nodes.statement: Let π be non-CM of weight k ≥ 2 with π_l non-supercuspidal for every l. Then there are a prime p > max(2(n + 1), (n − 1)k), ι, and π′ of weight k with r̄_{π,ι}(G_ℚ) ⊇ a conjugate of SL₂(F_p), π_p and π′_p unramified, r̄_{π,ι} ≅ r̄_{π′,ι}, and π′_l non-supercuspidal with all accessible refinements n-regular wherever π′_l is ramified.
hypotheses: π a cuspidal automorphic representation of GL₂(𝔸_ℚ), regular algebraic (from a holomorphic newform of weight k ≥ 2) unless said otherwise; r_{π,ι} : G_ℚ → GL₂(Q̄_p) its Galois representation (Tate-normalised: WD(r_{π,ι}|_{G_{ℚ_l}})^{F-ss} ≅ rec^T(ι^{−1}π_l)); n ≥ 2.
proofSteps: Choose p with large residual image (Ribet); change the level at each ramified l by level raising/lowering to reach n-regular refinements (NT I §8, not decomposed).
acceptance: Check the numerical bound p > (n − 1)k: it keeps Sym^{n−1} of the residual representation in the Fontaine–Laffaille range.

nodes.title: Symmetric powers when no local component is supercuspidal (NT I Theorem 8.1 = Theorem B, Corollary C)
nodes.statement: Let π be a non-CM regular algebraic cuspidal π of GL₂(𝔸_ℚ) such that π_l has nonzero Jacquet module for every prime l. Then for every n ≥ 3, Sym^{n−1}r_{π,ι} is automorphic, so Sym^{n−1}π exists. In particular (Corollary C) for a semistable elliptic curve E/ℚ the completed Λ(Sym^nE, s) is entire.
hypotheses: π a cuspidal automorphic representation of GL₂(𝔸_ℚ), regular algebraic (from a holomorphic newform of weight k ≥ 2) unless said otherwise; r_{π,ι} : G_ℚ → GL₂(Q̄_p) its Galois representation (Tate-normalised: WD(r_{π,ι}|_{G_{ℚ_l}})^{F-ss} ≅ rec^T(ι^{−1}π_l)); n ≥ 2.
proofSteps: Proposition 8.2 (all ramified refinements n-regular) by induction on the number of ramified primes, "killing ramification" along l-adic eigencurves (eigenvariety-propagation) down to level one (level-one-symmetric-powers).

General π: n-regular-congruences gives π′ satisfying 8.2 with r̄_{π,ι} ≅ r̄_{π′,ι} and large image; pd-automorphy-lifting (BLGGT Theorem 4.2.1) transfers automorphy of Sym^{n−1}r_{π′,ι} to Sym^{n−1}r_{π,ι}.
Corollary C: semistable E is modular (BCDT, Wiles) with Γ₀(N), N squarefree, so every π_l is unramified or Steinberg; Λ(Π, s) is entire for cuspidal Π (Godement–Jacquet, AL.2).
acceptance: Check that Γ₀(N) with N squarefree gives only unramified or Steinberg π_l, never supercuspidal.

sources.locator: §8, Theorem 8.1, p. 91; Introduction, Theorem B and Corollary C, p. 2 (arXiv v3)

nodes.title: Automorphy lifting for symmetric powers (NT II Theorem 2.1)
nodes.statement: Let π, π′ be regular algebraic cuspidal on GL₂(𝔸_F), F totally real, such that π′ has weight 2 and is non-CM, r_{π′,ι}|_{G_{F_v}} is not ordinary for v | p, r̄_{π′,ι} ≅ r̄_{π,ι}, π_v is a twist of Steinberg iff π′_v is (v ∤ p), and Sym^{n−1}r_{π′,ι} is automorphic. Then Sym^{n−1}r_{π,ι} is automorphic. No irreducibility of Sym^{n−1}r̄ is required (p ≤ n allowed).
hypotheses: π a cuspidal automorphic representation of GL₂(𝔸_ℚ), regular algebraic (from a holomorphic newform of weight k ≥ 2) unless said otherwise; r_{π,ι} : G_ℚ → GL₂(Q̄_p) its Galois representation (Tate-normalised: WD(r_{π,ι}|_{G_{ℚ_l}})^{F-ss} ≅ rec^T(ι^{−1}π_l)); n ≥ 2.
F totally real.
proofSteps: Reduce by soluble base change to conditions (6)–(11) of NT II p. 6, and pass to Π = π_K over a CM quadratic K.
Patch the map P → R from the pseudodeformation ring P of Sym^{n−1}r̄ to the deformation ring R of r̄: P_∞ → R_∞, with R_∞ a domain acting faithfully on patched rank-2 forms (Kisin).
Newton–Thorne 2020: Spec P is regular of dimension 0 at the pseudocharacter of Sym^{n−1}r_{π′,ι}, hence Spec P_∞ is regular there; so Spec R_∞ maps into the support of patched rank-n forms.
acceptance: Check that the theorem avoids killing the dual Selmer group of Sym^{n−1}r̄, which fails when p ≤ n.

sources.match: Theorem 2.1, the preliminary reductions and the patching argument sketched on pp. 2–3.

nodes.title: Symmetric power functoriality for all non-CM modular forms (NT II Theorem A, Corollary B)
nodes.statement: Let π be a regular algebraic, cuspidal, non-CM automorphic representation of GL₂(𝔸_ℚ). Then for every n ≥ 1, Sym^nπ exists as a regular algebraic cuspidal automorphic representation of GL_{n+1}(𝔸_ℚ). In particular (Corollary B), for every elliptic curve E/ℚ without CM and n ≥ 2, Λ(Sym^nE, s) is entire.
hypotheses: π a cuspidal automorphic representation of GL₂(𝔸_ℚ), regular algebraic (from a holomorphic newform of weight k ≥ 2) unless said otherwise; r_{π,ι} : G_ℚ → GL₂(Q̄_p) its Galois representation (Tate-normalised: WD(r_{π,ι}|_{G_{ℚ_l}})^{F-ss} ≅ rec^T(ι^{−1}π_l)); n ≥ 2.
proofSteps: Induction on #sc(π), the primes where π_p is supercuspidal; sc(π) = ∅ is non-supercuspidal-symmetric-powers.

Killing ramification: a "seasoned" good-dihedral π′ (with an auxiliary Steinberg prime r so that r_{π′,ι_q} has large image) congruent to π with sc(π′) = sc(π) ∖ {p}; symmetric-power-automorphy-lifting transfers automorphy (NT II Theorem 3.1, Propositions 3.7–3.11).
Corollary B: modularity of elliptic curves over ℚ (BCDT) and Godement–Jacquet.
acceptance: Check the scope: CM forms and weight-one forms are excluded here and handled by cm-and-weight-one-symmetric-powers.

sources.locator: Introduction, Theorem A and Corollary B, pp. 1–2; §3, Theorem 3.1, p. 20 (arXiv v2)

nodes.title: Symmetric powers of CM and weight-one forms (NT II Theorem A.1)
nodes.statement: Let π be cuspidal on GL₂(𝔸_ℚ) with π_∞ a holomorphic limit of discrete series, or π the automorphic induction of a Hecke character of a quadratic field. Then Sym^nπ exists for every n ≥ 1 (usually not cuspidal).
hypotheses: π as stated.
proofSteps: CM case: Sym^n of an induced representation decomposes into inductions of characters and characters.
Weight one: the Artin image is dihedral, tetrahedral, octahedral or icosahedral; the icosahedral case uses Kim–Shahidi tensor-product and symmetric-power functoriality (Kim 2004, Theorem 6.4; cited).
acceptance: Check the CM decomposition for n = 2 (symmetric-power-lifting test cm_not_cuspidal).

nodes.title: Equidistribution from L-functions (Kedlaya Theorem 24.2 and the Weyl criterion)
nodes.statement: Let K be a compact group with conjugacy-class space X, x_i ∈ X with norms N(x_i) ≥ 2, such that ∏(1 − N(x_i)^{−s})^{−1} converges for Re s > 1 and continues to a neighbourhood of Re s ≥ 1 with no zeros or poles except a simple pole at 1, and for each irreducible ρ, L(s, ρ) = ∏ det(1 − ρ(x_i)N(x_i)^{−s})^{−1} continues likewise with no zeros or poles on Re s ≥ 1 except possibly at 1. Then #{i : N(x_i) ≤ n} ~ n/log n, Σ_{N(x_i)≤n}χ(x_i) = c(χ)n/log n + o(n/log n) with −c(χ) the order of vanishing of L(s, ρ) at 1; if at most boundedly many x_i share a norm, the x_i are Haar-equidistributed iff c(χ) = 0 for every nontrivial irreducible χ (Peter–Weyl/Weyl criterion).
hypotheses: K a compact group (a compact Lie group in the application); ρ irreducible continuous representations.
proofSteps: Prime-number-theorem argument for each L(s, ρ): logarithmic derivative, Wiener–Ikehara (AnalyticNumberTheory AN.2), Kedlaya Theorem 24.2.
Peter–Weyl: finite linear combinations of irreducible characters are dense in the continuous class functions; orthogonality gives the integrals.
acceptance: Check the Chebotarev instance: K finite, ρ irreducible, recovering Kedlaya §22.5.

sources.locator: §§24.1–24.3, Theorem 24.1, Theorem 24.2 and Conjecture 24.3, printed pp. 133–134
sources.match: The equidistribution formalism (Conjecture 24.3 as printed is the criterion; see ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions/E6).

nodes.title: The Sato–Tate theorem for elliptic curves over ℚ
nodes.statement: Let E/ℚ be an elliptic curve without complex multiplication, and for good p let α_p be the root of X² − a_pX + p with nonnegative imaginary part and θ_p = arg(α_p/√p) ∈ [0, π]. Then (θ_p) is equidistributed for (2/π)sin²θ dθ, the push-forward of Haar measure on SU(2).
hypotheses: E/ℚ non-CM (End E = ℤ).
proofSteps: K = SU(2): classes are diag(e^{iθ}, e^{−iθ}), Haar measure is the Sato–Tate measure, and the irreducible representations are the Sym^n (Kedlaya §24.5).

L(s, Sym^n) = L(Sym^nE, s + n/2) (shift of the abscissa by n/2) is the L-function of the cuspidal Sym^nπ_E (non-cm-symmetric-powers), hence entire and nonvanishing on Re s ≥ 1 after the shift (Jacquet–Shalika, AL.3); for n ≥ 1 there is no pole, so c(χ) = 0.

Apply l-function-equidistribution-criterion. (Historically: Clozel–Harris–Shepherd-Barron–Taylor for non-integral j via potential automorphy; Barnet-Lamb–Geraghty–Harris–Taylor for all non-CM E over totally real fields.)
acceptance: Check the Haar-measure computation: the Weyl integration formula for SU(2) gives (2/π)sin²θ dθ on [0, π] (suggested file: the normalisation ∫₀^π sin²θ dθ = π/2).
Check that potential automorphy suffices: meromorphic continuation with no zeros or poles on Re s ≥ 1 (ML.2) already gives Sato–Tate; Newton–Thorne's entireness is not needed.

sourceIssues.locator: Chapter 24, §24.5, Theorem 24.6 and the preceding sentence, printed p. 135
sourceIssues.printed: The source claims that j(E) ∉ Z implies holomorphic continuation to C for ∏p Pn(p−s)−1. It also deduces nonvanishing on Re(s) ≥ 3/2 from absolute convergence of this Euler product on Re(s) > 3/2.
sourceIssues.correction: The work of Clozel–Harris–Shepherd-Barron–Taylor gives meromorphic continuation, holomorphic and nonvanishing on Re s ≥ 1 + n/2, which suffices for Sato–Tate; holomorphy on all of ℂ was proved later (Newton–Thorne 2021, for all non-CM E). The Euler product converges absolutely for Re s > 1 + n/2, not 3/2, and the shift of the abscissa is n/2, not 1/2.
sourceIssues.reason: P_n has roots α_p^{n−j}ᾱ_p^j of absolute value p^{n/2}, so the abscissa of absolute convergence is 1 + n/2 (3/2 only for n = 1). Entireness of the symmetric power L-functions was open until Newton–Thorne (their Corollary C and NT II Corollary B), whose introductions state that only meromorphic continuation was previously known.
searched: 2026-09-29: author page and the notes' front matter (no erratum list); Newton–Thorne I introduction p. 2 confirms what was known before 2019.
